prompt: What is a good durable workflow engine for AI tasks with retries?

result.text:
When building AI workflows (multi-step LLM calls, tool-use loops, human-in-the-loop approvals, or long-running agent tasks), a durable workflow engine prevents losing state when an API times out, a model hallucinates, or a server crashes.

The top options vary depending on your stack, whether you want code-first vs. serverless, and how deeply you are building AI agents:

Top Durable Workflow Engines for AI

Inngest (Best all-around for TypeScript/Python & AI agents)

Why it fits AI: Features built-in step controls, streaming support, easy handling of rate limits/backpressure, and high developer satisfaction for agentic loops.
Retries & Durability: 4 default retries with custom onFailure handlers, step-by-step memoization, and great visibility via their dashboard.
Get started: Check out Inngest.

Temporal (Best for heavy, complex, mission-critical distributed systems)

Why it fits AI: The gold standard for ultra-reliable state management. If your AI workflow spans days, interacts with external Webhooks, or requires complex compensation logic (Sagas), Temporal won't drop a bit.
Retries & Durability: Workflows run as code; activities retry indefinitely (or with granular backoff policies) by default. Steep learning curve, requires running Temporal Server (or Temporal Cloud).
Get started: Explore Temporal.io.

Trigger.dev (Best for AI-native and background job integration)

Why it fits AI: Built specifically to handle long-running code execution (like running heavy Python/TS scripts, scraping, or multi-model chains) without hitting serverless timeouts.
Retries & Durability: 3 default attempts with a visual dashboard for bulk-replaying failed runs.
Get started: See Trigger.dev.

Upstash Workflow (Best for Edge/Serverless & HTTP-based setups)

Why it fits AI: Zero-infrastructure, queue-less workflow engine that works over simple HTTP endpoints (great for Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, or Deno Deploy).
Retries & Durability: Retries each step 3 times with exponential backoff; if it permanently fails, it pushes to a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) where you can resume or restart from specific steps.
Get started: Read the Upstash Workflow Docs.

Restate / DBOS (Best for transactional consistency & database-backed state)

Why it fits AI: Treats application code like a database transaction—if an AI step crashes halfway, it rolls back or resumes deterministically without duplicate side-effects (like double-charging an API or sending duplicate emails).
Get started: Check out Restate.dev or DBOS.dev.
